subject: MAP: CuraCloud performance roadmap + TTFT streaming plan
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: sara.liu@curacloud.com, tom.hastings@curacloud.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + TTFT streaming benchmarking approach

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Attached is a first-draft Mutual Action Plan (Cura_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a companion test plan (ttft_streaming_test_plan.md) that outlines how we'll validate streaming TTFT (time-to-first-token) and tail latencies for your chat workflows. High-level ask: can you review the MAP milestones and confirm the expected decision-makers for procurement and security?

What we propose in the MAP for the performance validation phase:
- Objective: Demonstrate <200ms p50 TTFT and <600ms p95 for typical 512-token chat prompts at 50 concurrent users using our hosted inference with streaming.
- Tests: incremental concurrency sweep (1, 10, 50, 100), token-length matrix (64 / 256 / 512), p50/p95/p99 reporting for TTFT and per-token streaming latency.
- Success criteria: p95 TTFT under 700ms in your EU/US regions, no regression >10% vs baseline throughput, and consistent KV-cache hit rate >90%.
- Deliverables: raw CSVs, summary chart, and a short executive slide with recommended serving knobs (batching, quantization profile).

Timing: we can run the initial sweep next week (Mar 23–24) if you can provide a small sample prompt set and a sandbox account for traffic. I've put tentative dates in the MAP.

I've looped in Aditya (infra lead) who will own the test harness and Marissa (solutions) for instrumentation and eval probes.

Next steps: please confirm SLA/region constraints and whether you want us to include a dedicated GPU backbone test vs hosted fallbacks.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director of Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: Cura_MAP_v1.xlsx; ttft_streaming_test_plan.md
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@curacloud.com>

Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, tom.hastings@curacloud.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft + TTFT streaming benchmarking approach

Karthik —

Thanks for the plan and the clear success criteria. A couple quick clarifications before we lock dates:
1) Region: primary traffic will be US-west; we may want a single sanity check in eu-west. Can you include region tags in the CSV outputs?
2) Dataset: we'll share a 150-prompt sample (mix of short discovery + long context). Can you confirm tokenization and whether you include pre-prompt system messages in TTFT?
3) Security: procurement will need the SOC2 evidence; are you able to provide the audit artifact during the MAP window?

Procurement: Tom will own the contract side; he asks for an estimate of total test-hours for budgeting.

If we can confirm by EOD today, we'll slot your run on Mar 23.

-Sara
Sara Liu
Head of Platform — CuraCloud
sara.liu@curacloud.com

Sara / Tom —

Quick answers:
- Region tags: yes, we'll emit a region column and separate CSVs for us-west and eu-west sanity check.
- Tokenization: we'll include both raw prompt token count and the effective model-token count after tokenization; system messages are included in model context for TTFT measurements (we'll provide both numbers).
- SOC2 evidence: we can provide the SOC2 scope doc and a redacted report snapshot; I'll surface the artifact in the shared Drive link and add to the MAP milestones for "Security evidence handover" on Mar 24.

Estimate of test-hours: for the full matrix (concurrency x token-length x 3 runs each) plan for ~10 hours of continuous testing, engineering ramp and post-analysis ~8 hours. Budget estimate: ~18 engineer-hours + ephemeral GPU cost (we'll provide a cost estimate line item in the MAP).
